description: Experience the rich, smoky flavors of authentic Tandoori Chicken, perfected on a charcoal grill. This traditional Indian dish features succulent chicken marinated in a vibrant blend of yogurt and aromatic spices, then cooked to tender perfection over glowing coals. A true culinary delight that brings the essence of Indian street food right to your backyard.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken and First Marinade
instructions.text: Wash and pat dry the chicken thoroughly. Make deep gashes all over the chicken pieces with a sharp knife. In a large bowl, combine ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, Kashmiri red chili powder, and salt. Rub this mixture generously all over the chicken, making sure it gets into the gashes. Let it marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.

instructions.title: Prepare the Second Marinade
instructions.text: In a separate bowl, whisk together the thick plain yogurt, garam masala, cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, and tandoori masala (if using). Add a pinch of red food color if desired for the classic tandoori look. Mix until well combined and smooth.

instructions.title: Combine Marinades and Chill
instructions.text: Add the second marinade mixture to the chicken, ensuring every piece is thoroughly coated. Massage the marinade into the chicken. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, or preferably overnight, for the best flavor and tenderness. The longer the marination, the better the results.

instructions.title: Prepare the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: About 30-45 minutes before grilling, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the charcoal for direct medium-high heat. Once the coals are glowing red with a light ash coating, place the grill grate over them. Clean the grate and brush it with a little oil to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the Tandoori Chicken
instructions.text: Remove the chicken from the marinade, letting any excess drip off. Place the chicken pieces directly over the hot coals. Grill for about 25-35 minutes, turning every 5-7 minutes to ensure even cooking and charring. Baste with mustard oil or melted butter during the last 10 minutes of grilling to keep it moist and add flavor.

instructions.title: Check for Doneness and Serve
instructions.text: The chicken is cooked when its internal temperature reaches 74°C (165°F) and the juices run clear. You should see beautiful char marks on the outside. Remove the chicken from the grill, transfer to a platter, and let it rest for a few minutes. Garnish with fresh onion rings, lemon wedges, and chopped cilantro. Serve hot with mint chutney or raita.

tips: For truly authentic flavor, ensure your yogurt is thick; drain it in a muslin cloth for an hour or two to remove excess water before mixing the marinade.
Do not skip the deep gashes on the chicken; these allow the marinade to penetrate deeply, ensuring juicy and flavorful meat.
Always let the charcoal reach the right temperature before placing the chicken; this prevents the chicken from sticking and ensures proper charring without burning.
article:
Unleash the vibrant flavors of India right in your backyard with a dish that’s as exciting to make as it is to eat: Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled. This iconic Indian dinner recipe brings together succulent chicken, a rich, spicy yogurt marinade, and the irresistible smoky char that only charcoal grilling can deliver. Forget ordering takeout; mastering this dish at home is simpler than you think and promises an unforgettable culinary experience.

The magic of Tandoori Chicken lies in its deep, complex flavors and tender texture, traditionally achieved in a cylindrical clay oven called a tandoor. While most home cooks don't have a tandoor, a charcoal grill is the next best thing, perfectly replicating that smoky, slightly charred exterior and juicy interior. Get ready to transform your regular barbecue into an exotic feast!

## What is Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken?

Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is a classic North Indian dish featuring chicken marinated in a mixture of yogurt and a potent blend of spices, then cooked over high heat. The yogurt acts as a tenderizer, while the spices – including ginger, garlic, garam masala, cumin, coriander, and often Kashmiri chili powder for color and mild heat – infuse the meat with incredible depth. Traditionally, the chicken cooks quickly in a tandoor, achieving a distinct smoky flavor and a beautiful reddish hue, often enhanced by food coloring.

When prepared on a charcoal grill, the chicken gains an authentic smoky essence that mirrors the tandoor's effect. The direct heat from the charcoal sears the outside, creating a flavorful crust while keeping the inside moist and tender. This method allows the marinade to caramelize beautifully, yielding a dish that's aromatic, spicy, and incredibly satisfying. It's a cornerstone of Indian cuisine, celebrated for its robust flavors and appealing presentation.

## Ingredients You Need for Tandoori Chicken

To create an authentic and delicious Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken, gather the following ingredients:

For the Chicken:
*   2 lbs bone-in, skinless chicken pieces (thighs, drumsticks, or a mix)

For the Marinade:
*   1 cup plain Greek yogurt (full-fat works best)
*   2 tablespoons fresh ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice
*   1 tablespoon Kashmiri chili powder (or paprika for less heat, plus a pinch of red food coloring if desired)
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1/2 teaspoon black pepper
*   1/2 teaspoon salt (or to taste)
*   1 tablespoon mustard oil or vegetable oil
*   Optional: 1/4 teaspoon red food coloring (for that signature vibrant red)

For Grilling & Serving:
*   Melted butter or ghee for basting
*   Lemon wedges, fresh cilantro for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Grilling

Making Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is a process that rewards patience and attention to detail. Follow these steps for perfect results:

1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Rinse the chicken pieces and pat them thoroughly dry. Using a sharp knife, make 2-3 deep slits on each piece of chicken. This allows the marinade to penetrate deeply and helps the chicken cook evenly.
2.  **Make the Marinade:** In a large bowl, combine the Greek yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, Kashmiri chili powder, cumin, coriander, garam masala, turmeric, black pepper, salt, mustard oil (or vegetable oil), and optional red food coloring. Mix everything until well combined and smooth.
3.  **Marinate the Chicken:** Add the prepared chicken pieces to the marinade, ensuring each piece is thoroughly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or ideally overnight (up to 24 hours). The longer the marination, the more tender and flavorful your chicken will be.
4.  **Prepare Your Charcoal Grill:** About 30-40 minutes before you plan to cook, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the charcoal for two-zone cooking: pile most of the coals on one side for direct high heat, and leave the other side empty for indirect medium heat. The coals should be glowing and covered with a light layer of ash. Clean and oil your grill grates to prevent sticking.
5.  **Grill the Chicken:** Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the hot coals. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side to get a nice char and color. Then, move the chicken to the indirect heat zone. Close the grill lid and continue to cook, turning occasionally, for 20-30 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C). During the last 5-10 minutes of cooking, you can baste the chicken with melted butter or ghee to add richness and shine.
6.  **Rest and Serve:** Once cooked, remove the Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5-10 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring moist and tender chicken.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving restaurant-quality Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled at home requires a few expert tricks:

*   **Marination is Key:** Do not skimp on marination time. The yogurt and acid not only tenderize but also infuse maximum flavor. Overnight marination is truly worth the wait.
*   **Bone-in, Skinless Chicken:** Bone-in chicken retains moisture better and offers more flavor. Skinless is preferred for Tandoori as the marinade adheres directly to the meat, and the skin can become rubbery.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Grill:** Cook in batches if necessary. Overcrowding drops the grill temperature and steams the chicken instead of grilling it, preventing that coveted char.
*   **Temperature Control:** Start with high heat for searing, then move to indirect heat to cook through without burning. This mimics the tandoor's intense, even heat.
*   **Rest Your Chicken:** Always let grilled chicken rest. It's crucial for juicy results.
*   **Charcoal Type:** Use good quality lump charcoal for a cleaner, more intense smoky flavor compared to briquettes. You can also add a few wood chips (like apple or mesquite) soaked in water to the coals for an extra layer of smokiness.
*   **Food Coloring:** While optional, a tiny bit of red food coloring (or more Kashmiri chili powder) helps achieve the iconic vibrant red color without significantly altering taste.

## Serving Suggestions

Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled is a showstopper on its own, but it truly shines when paired with complementary Indian dishes:

*   **Naan Bread or Roti:** Tear off pieces of warm, fresh naan or roti to scoop up the chicken and any remaining juices.
*   **Mint-Cilantro Chutney:** A refreshing, zesty chutney provides a lovely contrast to the rich chicken.
*   **Raita:** A cooling yogurt-based dip, often made with cucumber and mint, helps balance the spices.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** A squeeze of fresh lemon juice just before eating brightens all the flavors.
*   **Basmati Rice:** A side of fluffy basmati rice is perfect for soaking up the delicious marinade.
*   **Kachumber Salad:** A simple salad of chopped cucumber, tomato, onion, and cilantro offers a fresh crunch.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is divine, don't hesitate to experiment:

*   **Different Cuts of Chicken:** Boneless chicken thighs or breasts can be used, though they will cook faster. Adjust grilling time accordingly. For boneless pieces, marinate for a minimum of 2-4 hours.
*   **Vegetarian Options:** The Tandoori marinade is incredibly versatile. Try it with paneer (Indian cheese), firm tofu, mushrooms, bell peppers, or cauliflower florets for a delicious vegetarian grill. Marinate these for 1-2 hours.
*   **Marinade Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of chili powder to suit your preference for heat. For a less spicy version, use paprika instead of Kashmiri chili powder.
*   **Grill Alternatives:** If a charcoal grill isn't available, you can still achieve great results.
    *   **Gas Grill:** Follow similar steps, creating direct and indirect heat zones. You might miss some of the charcoal smokiness, but it will still be delicious.
    *   **Oven:** Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 25-35 minutes, then broil for 3-5 minutes to get some char. Use a wire rack over a baking sheet to allow even cooking.
    *   **Grill Pan:** For smaller batches, a cast-iron grill pan can work on the stovetop, though it won't give the same smoky flavor.

Embrace the smoky allure of Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken and bring the authentic tastes of an Indian restaurant right to your home. This flavorful dish is more than just a meal; it's an experience, promising tender, spice-infused chicken with that irresistible char. Perfect for family dinners or entertaining guests, this Indian dinner recipe is sure to become a cherished favorite.
